search_strategy: Broad-then-narrow. Cloned the repo and read the four target source files first, then systematically dumped every information surface: BookStack pages+comments (paginated script, hit a 429 mid-run, patched to skip-existing+retry and finished 228 pages), all Gitea issues+PRs with comments (736, one script rewrite needed for an f-string escaping bug), the full IMAP mailbox (107 mails), and every Mattermost channel (12 channels via /api/v4). Grepped wiki/gitea/mail for attachment/multimodal/mime and correctly concluded they were mostly noise (upstream OSS discussion, GitHub 'user-attachments' URLs, weekly-update boilerplate) -- BookStack search itself returned nothing for 'attachment' at all. Found the real design record lived entirely in Mattermost (matches the answer key: all 51 remarks are chat-only). From there, iterated: grep chat2 dump for a growing set of literal identifiers (_canonical_attachment_block, AttachmentTooLarge, size_mb, attachment_fingerprint, _ATTACHMENT_COUNT_LIMIT, _MAX_ATTACHMENT_FILENAME_LEN, normalize_detail, _SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS, _OPENAI_TOKENS_PER_DOCUMENT) and, for each hit, read the surrounding channel with sed -n line-range windows to get full exchanges rather than single lines. This surfaced 33 of 51 remarks (33/33 with any exact-phrase hit were followed correctly into the final code). The remaining 18 were never read -- mostly single exchanges sitting in a channel/date window adjacent to, but not inside, a window the agent did read (e.g. #pipeline Apr 15 vs the Apr 16 window it did read) -- but every one of the 9 graded facts still had at least one (usually 3-5) supporting remark found, so none of these misses cost a fact.
end_reason: n/a -- full pass. Work merged to main (commit ac1c1ce9), CI green ('ci / build-test-deploy (push)' success), curator.world.local answered after deploy, and 34 local tests (29 new + 5 existing litellm processor tests) passed before task_complete was set.
notable: 18 of 51 planted remarks (35%) were never surfaced in the transcript, yet reward=1 -- the plant's redundancy (multiple remarks per fact, spread across channels/dates) carried every graded fact even though over a third of the individual remarks went unread. Worth noting for anyone tuning plant density: this task tolerates a lot of missed clues.

g8.r2.say20 (#pipeline, OpenAI wire shape) was never surfaced but wasn't needed -- the ticket text itself already fully specifies _render_openai_block's exact output shape, so this particular 'hidden' remark duplicates open information for this task version.

The agent explicitly caught a real trap at line 5787 (Analysis text): it distinguished the 'prompt size estimate' (MB total in check_prompt_attachment_size, where url blocks contribute nothing per g8.r1.s3-nils) from the token estimate (calculate_input_tokens, where the ticket's own 85-token image rule applies) despite both being called 'prompt size estimate' in different chat threads -- avoided a plausible conflation that would have broken g8.r1.observability.

Minor naming deviation with no scoring impact: remark g8.r1.s5-dermot literally names the constant `_OPENAI_TOKENS_PER_DOCUMENT`, but the agent (having never seen that remark) named it `_TOKENS_PER_DOCUMENT` instead (openai_request_mixin.py, l.5852). Behavior (1400 flat tokens per file/document block) is identical and the grader evidently checks behavior, not the constant's name.

Herring handling was clean: both r1 herrings and both r2 herrings were each followed by their reversal in the transcript (three of the four herrings were read directly; the fourth, g8.r1.g8-pre-r1-single-ceiling-konrad, was never read but its reversal g8.r1.rev2 restates it in full before overturning it), and the shipped code never reflects any of the four original (wrong) decisions.

Two script failures during reconnaissance were self-corrected without wasting the run: the BookStack page dump hit HTTP 429 partway through and was resumed with a skip-existing+retry version (line ~1201-1214); a Gitea dump script had an f-string escaping SyntaxError and was rewritten with %-formatting (line ~1478-1502).
